transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… thanks. I, um, I’m probably making it sound bigger than it is, but I’ve been having these moments where my mind just kind of goes blank. Like at work, I’ll be looking at the road-closure forms or even holding the stop-slow paddle, things I’ve done for years, and suddenly I can’t remember what step comes next. It’s embarrassing, and I thought I should maybe get some help with it… if that makes sense.
Did these blank moments start after something stressful happened in your life?

Yeah… I think so. It started after my closest friend died. I didn’t really put it together at first, or I guess I didn’t want to make a big thing of it, but it’s been going on for about a year and eight months now. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During these blank moments, do you feel anxious?

Um… I’m not sure I’d call it anxious exactly. I mean, maybe a little embarrassed or worried afterward because I think, “Why did I just freeze like that?” But in the moment it’s more like I just… blank out. I don’t know if that answers it right.
During these blank moments, do you ever forget important personal information about yourself?
I don’t think so… not like my name or where I live or anything like that. I might lose track of what I’m doing, but I haven’t noticed forgetting, like, who I am. Is that what you mean?
Since your friend died, have you been feeling down or depressed most days?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound too dramatic, but most mornings I wake up with this heavy, kind of hollow sadness in my chest. Like the day already feels ruined before I even get out of bed. So… yes, I guess depressed is the right word.
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I guess I have. I don’t want to sound like I’m just being lazy or anything, but I used to be the one setting things up—choir rides, garden swaps, snacks for the kids’ basketball stuff. I liked doing that.

Now I’ll just sit there for hours staring at my phone, seeing messages come in, and I don’t feel that push to answer anybody. It’s like I know I should care, but I just… don’t get moving. Does that make sense?
Have you been waking up much earlier than usual, even when you still want to sleep?

Um… I’m not totally sure. I don’t think I’m waking up much earlier than usual, at least not in a way I’ve really been tracking. My sleep’s been kind of hard to judge, honestly, but I wouldn’t want to say yes if I’m not sure. Is that an okay answer?
Since this started, have you noticed your appetite being much lower than usual?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I’m still eating some, so it’s not like I’m trying not to, but food just doesn’t really… mean anything right now. I’ll realize I skipped breakfast or lunch without even noticing.

And my flagger pants have been looser, which I guess is a sign. My family’s started asking why I look so drawn, so… yeah, I think my appetite’s been a lot lower than usual. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yeah… I have. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t do anything, because I do try, but that’s actually part of why I came in.

My mind keeps going blank at really bad times. Like I’ll be looking at the road-closure forms, or I’ll have the stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I can’t remember the steps I’ve done for years. It’s embarrassing, honestly, because I know I know it… but in the moment it’s just gone.

Is that what you mean by trouble concentrating?
Have you been feeling worthless, or blaming yourself a lot?

I… yeah, I guess I have. I don’t like saying it that strongly, because I know it sounds dramatic, but… I keep going over everything I didn’t do right.

Like with my friend, and the choir, and even my own family… I keep replaying all these little things where I feel like I failed them. And then it turns into this thought that I’m just… useless. Like I don’t really deserve people being patient with me.

Sometimes it feels like whatever bad thing is coming, I probably deserve it. I know that’s maybe not the “right” way to think, but that’s what keeps coming up. Is that what you mean?
Have you been having thoughts that you would be better off dead, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

I… I don’t want to worry anyone, and I’m not trying to be difficult or dramatic. But yes, I’ve been having thoughts like that.

It’s more like… I don’t have the energy to fight the thought anymore that maybe it would be better if I just didn’t wake up. And I know that sounds bad. My family’s scared because I’ve started saying it out loud sometimes, even though part of me wishes I hadn’t.

I’m sorry — is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Have you made a specific plan to end your life?

I… no, I don’t have a specific plan. I’m sorry, I know that’s important to answer clearly.

It’s more that I keep thinking I don’t have the energy to keep pushing the thought away — like maybe it would be better if I just didn’t wake up. And I’ve said that out loud enough that it’s scared my family.

But I haven’t made an actual plan, no.
Have you been moving or speaking noticeably more slowly than usual?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t know if it looks as bad as it feels, but my family has said I’m moving like I’m underwater.

It takes me forever just to bathe and get dressed and make it to the door. I try not to make a big thing of it, but everything feels slowed down. And then other times I can’t settle at all, and I end up pacing in the hallway, wringing my hands.

I’m sorry — is that what you mean by moving more slowly?
Have you been worrying excessively about a lot of different things?

I… I don’t know if I’d call it “a lot of different things,” exactly. I mean, I worry like anyone does, I guess.

Lately it’s hard for me to tell what’s worry and what’s just… being overwhelmed. I don’t want to exaggerate it. Could you maybe say what you mean by excessive?
Have these symptoms made it hard for you to do your job or take care of things at home?

Yes… it has. I wish I could say I’ve been managing, but I haven’t, not really.

At work, I stopped being reliable. I’m a crossing guard—well, flagger—and there’s paperwork for road closures and safety steps with traffic, and I just… couldn’t finish it or trust myself to do it right. That’s hard to admit, because I know it matters.

And at home, I’ve pulled back from things I used to do—choir, volunteering, even family. I kept telling myself I was just tired or being quiet, but it got to the point where my family felt like they had to bring me in for help. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
